spatial_claims.claim: Triangles ABC and DCE placed together at vertex C; B, C, D collinear on a single straight line
A and E lie on opposite sides of line BD
Angles BCA and DCE described as vertical angles at C (anticipates conclusion, not used as premise)
Line AE crosses line BD at point G (existence from opposite-side condition)
BD is a transversal to parallel lines AB and DE; alternate angles ABG = EDG by I.29
Lines AE and BD intersect at G producing vertical angles AGB = EGD
Triangles ABG and EDG are equiangular
AB/ED = BG/GD from equiangular triangles by 6.4
G lies on segment BD between B and D, so BG + GD = BD
C lies between B and D on line BD, so BC + CD = BD
G and C both on segment BD at equal distance from D (GD = CD), so G coincides with C
Since G = C, line AE passes through C, making A, C, E collinear

configuration_map: Line BD is the base. C lies between B and D on this line (BC and CD are sides of the respective triangles). A lies on one side of line BD (vertex of triangle ABC), E lies on the opposite side (vertex of triangle DCE). AB is parallel to DE. Point G is constructed as the intersection of line AE with line BD. Since A and E are on opposite sides, G exists and a coordinate analysis confirms G lies strictly between B and D. The proportionality BG/GD = BC/CD (derived from the given BC/CD = AB/DE and the equiangular-triangle result AB/DE = BG/GD) forces G = C, establishing that A, C, E are collinear.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof constructs a coherent configuration with B, C, D collinear and A, E on opposite sides. The auxiliary point G (intersection of AE with BD) is correctly shown to lie between B and D, and the proportionality argument validly demonstrates G = C. The vertical angles remark in Step 1 anticipates the conclusion but is never used as a premise in the logical chain, so it introduces no circularity. No angle decomposition errors, no inside/outside contradictions, no ray-ordering inconsistencies.
